title: Shared state
description:
Write a thread-safe word counter that many threads can share, and a parallel word count built on it:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct Counter { inner: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, u64>>> }

impl Counter {
    fn new() -> Self
    fn add(&self, word: &str, n: u64)            // note: &self, not &mut self
    fn get(&self, word: &str) -> u64
    fn snapshot(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, u64>  // a sorted copy
}

fn count_words(lines: &[&str], threads: usize) -> BTreeMap<String, u64>   // lower-case words, split on non-letters
struct Hits { total: AtomicU64 }                                          // a lock-free counter
```

- Cloning a `Counter` gives another handle to the **same** counts.
- `count_words` gives each scoped thread a share of the lines; each thread counts into its **own** local `HashMap` and adds its totals to a shared `Counter` once at the end (so it locks once per word per thread, not once per word occurrence).
- `Hits` has `new()`, `hit(&self)` and `get(&self) -> u64`.

The tests need `use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};`, `use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};` and `use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` at the top of your file.
hints: The `Arc` lets every clone point to the same `Mutex`; `add` takes `&self` because the mutex, not the borrow checker, controls changes.

`split` also accepts a closure that says which characters separate the pieces, and `c.is_alphabetic()` tells whether a `char` is a letter: `line.to_lowercase().split(|c: char| !c.is_alphabetic())` gives the words, plus some empty pieces to filter out.
Counting into a thread-local `HashMap` first and merging once per thread keeps the lock almost always free: the threads spend their time counting, not waiting.
lessonTitle: Shared State with Arc and Mutex
